fields.Name: IT69 - Layered Base Views
fields.Description: Proves the LAYERED base view arrangement (Entity.GeneratedBaseViewName) against a live database rather than a hand-built EntityInfo. Deterministic, read-only, LLM-free, SQL Server only — CodeGen refuses layering on PostgreSQL, where every check skips-as-pass. LBV1 layering metadata is coherent (BaseViewGenerated=0, BaseView set, names distinct, EntityInfo.GeneratedViewName agrees with the declared column); LBV2 both the inner and outer views physically exist as distinct objects; LBV3 the outer view actually selects FROM the inner one, i.e. it is genuinely a wrapper and everything underneath keeps regenerating; LBV4 CodeGen has not overwritten the application-owned outer view — the failure that would destroy hand-written SQL on a routine codegen run; LBV5 every inner-view column is inherited by the outer view, catching a wrapper that stopped doing SELECT g.* and would silently drop newly generated columns; LBV6 a CodeGen-generated column that is NOT a base-table column reaches the public surface, is registered as a virtual EntityField, and is selectable through RunView. Anti-vacuity: the bundle fails rather than skips when no entity declares GeneratedBaseViewName, since MJ core ships layered entities as of v6.1. 6 checks LBV1-LBV6.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: All 6 checks pass against a database built from migrations + metadata: layering metadata coherent, inner and outer views both present and distinct, outer view wraps the inner one and shows no sign of being overwritten by CodeGen, every generated column reaches the public surface, and at least one CodeGen-generated column is proven queryable via RunView.
